source: GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit), Support of Regional Economic Cooperation in Asia (SRECA), in cooperation with MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture — គោលការណ៍ណែនាំអំពីការនាំចេញផ្លែស្វាយស្រស់ពីប្រទេសកម្ពុជាទៅប្រទេសចិន (Guideline on Fresh Mango Export from Cambodia to China), Final Version, Phnom Penh, December 2020, 67pp
text:
Packaging, labeling, and border-crossing compliance requirements for mango exported to China, per the GIZ/SRECA guideline (December 2020 edition).

Wood packaging material (e.g., wooden crates or pallets used in shipment) must comply with the international standard ISPM-15, meaning the wood must be heat-treated (or otherwise treated) and stamped accordingly by a GACC-recognized facility; untreated or improperly marked wood packaging is a common cause of shipment delay or rejection at the Chinese border.

At the border, Chinese customs/quarantine officers may conduct physical inspection of a sample of crates from each shipment to confirm that the product's declared quantity, weight, and condition match the accompanying documents (the source notes a benchmark example of officers checking around 3 crates per roughly every 5 tons of declared product, though exporters should confirm current inspection ratios with GACC or their customs broker).

Exporters are advised to ensure that only registered, GACC-approved packing houses and orchards supply product for a given shipment, and that the packing house's own phytosanitary and quality-control procedures are followed consistently, since inconsistent or unregistered sourcing can jeopardize the shipment's clearance even if the paperwork looks correct on its face.

Labeling should clearly and accurately identify the product, origin orchard/registration number, and packing house, consistent with what is declared in the customs and phytosanitary documents — mismatched or vague labeling is flagged as a common avoidable cause of delay.
